title: Wrap-Around Dial
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Clocks and Watches with AI
description: A clock-style dial for 12, 24 or 60 positions shows (x + step) % n step by step, including how Python wraps negative numbers.

learningObjectives: Apply the modulo operator to predict where a counter lands after adding or subtracting
Explain why (x + step) % n always gives a value from 0 to n - 1
Predict the result of going backward past zero, such as (0 - 1) % 60 = 59
prerequisites: The % operator from the arithmetic section of Chapter 3

accessibility.notes: Controls are standard HTML form elements; the canvas has a describe() text for screen readers

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Practice with immediate visual feedback and prediction
keyQuestions: What is the largest value (x + step) % n can have?
How many times did the pointer pass 0 when 68 became 8?
commonMisconceptions: A wrap needs an if statement to reset the counter
assessmentOpportunities: Students predict at least 8 of 10 results correctly in Predict mode.
Students explain why the result can never equal n.
Students write `minute = (minute - 1) % 60` for a down button without help.

controls.label: Reset
controls.description: Returns x to its starting value

controls.label: Predict
controls.description: Asks for the result before the pointer moves

controls.label: Check
controls.description: Checks the prediction and moves the pointer
